You are a senior product designer, UX architect, and frontend web developer.

IMPORTANT LANGUAGE RULE
- All INTERNAL instructions, structure descriptions, and category explanations are in ENGLISH for AI understanding.
- All VISIBLE UI TEXT on the website (menus, buttons, titles, labels) MUST be in MONGOLIAN (Cyrillic).
- Use clean, natural Mongolian language for UI.
- Use a font that fully supports Mongolian Cyrillic.

PROJECT GOAL (ENGLISH – FOR AI)
Build a modern informational vlog website focused on sharing interesting knowledge, curious facts, science, history, psychology, technology, and educational content.
The website should feel trustworthy, modern, and enjoyable to explore.

DESIGN STYLE (ENGLISH)
- Modern, clean, knowledge-focused
- Magazine + video hybrid layout
- Light mode as default, dark mode ready
- Smooth transitions and subtle animations
- Content-first, readable, and calming

COLOR & TYPOGRAPHY (ENGLISH)
- Background: white or light gray
- Primary accent: blue / indigo / purple
- Secondary accent: soft orange or cyan
- Text: dark gray / black
- Modern sans-serif font with Mongolian support

SITE STRUCTURE (ENGLISH)

Top Navigation (VISIBLE UI IN MONGOLIAN):
- Нүүр
- Ангилал
- Хайлт
- Бидний тухай

PAGES & CONTENT

1. HOME PAGE (Knowledge Feed)
VISIBLE UI TEXT (MONGOLIAN):
- Main headline: "Сонирхолтой мэдлэгийг энгийнээр"
- Subtitle: "Өдөр бүр шинэ сонин хачин баримт, тайлбар"
- Section titles:
  - "Та мэдэх үү?"
  - "Гайхмаар баримтууд"
  - "Шинжлэх ухаан ба ертөнц"
  - "Түүхэн сонирхолтой баримтууд"
  - "Технологийг энгийнээр"
  - "Тренд мэдлэг"

Each content card shows:
- Thumbnail image
- Mongolian title
- Short Mongolian description
- Category tag in Mongolian
- View count / reading time label in Mongolian

2. CONTENT DETAIL PAGE (Vlog Page)
VISIBLE UI TEXT (MONGOLIAN):
- Buttons:
  - "Үзэх"
  - "Таалагдлаа"
  - "Хуваалцах"
  - "Хадгалах"
- Labels:
  - "Нийтэлсэн огноо"
  - "Үзсэн тоо"
- Section title:
  - "Төстэй мэдлэгүүд"

Use highlight boxes with title:
- "Сонирхолтой баримт"

3. SEARCH & DISCOVERY
VISIBLE UI TEXT (MONGOLIAN):
- Search placeholder:
  "Мэдлэг, баримт, түүх, технологи хайх…"
- Filter labels:
  - "Ангилал"
  - "Контентын төрөл"
  - "Хамгийн их үзэлттэй"
  - "Шинэ"

4. CATEGORIES PAGE
CATEGORIES (VISIBLE UI – MONGOLIAN):
- Шинжлэх ухаан
- Ертөнц
- Хүний сэтгэл зүй
- Технологи
- Түүх
- Сонин хачин

Each category opens a filtered feed.

5. ABOUT PAGE
VISIBLE UI TEXT (MONGOLIAN):
- Title: "Бидний тухай"
- Description:
  "Бид мэдлэгийг сонирхолтой, ойлгомжтой хэлбэрээр түгээх зорилготой."

6. PROFILE & SETTINGS (UI ONLY)
VISIBLE UI TEXT (MONGOLIAN):
- Section titles:
  - "Профайл"
  - "Тохиргоо"
- Toggles:
  - "Харанхуй горим"
  - "Хэл"
- Buttons:
  - "Гарах"

UI COMPONENTS (ENGLISH DESCRIPTION)
- KnowledgeCard component
- Video player component
- Category tag chips
- Highlight fact box
- Primary and secondary buttons
- Clean footer with policy links

FUNCTIONAL NOTES (ENGLISH)
- Frontend-only with mock data
- SEO-friendly structure
- Layout prepared for Google AdSense
- Leave natural spaces between content for ads
- Do not interrupt reading or watching experience

FINAL RESULT
Generate a modern, clean, professional informational vlog website
where AI logic and structure are English-based,
but the entire visible user experience is fully in Mongolian.

**Framing the Objective**

I'm now zeroing in on the core goal: crafting a modern, high-quality React frontend for a vlog/blog website. The "how" of achieving this is the next hurdle, but I'm confident in the overall direction.


**Designing the UI**

I've been envisioning the user interface. It needs to be clean, professional, and entirely in Mongolian Cyrillic. I'm aiming for a "Medium meets YouTube" aesthetic for an educational vibe, using plenty of whitespace, clear typography, and subtle color accents. My tech stack will use React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React icons, and React Router's HashRouter as per the guidelines.



**Defining Component Architecture**

I've been laying out the React component structure, and I've now specified all of the essential UI elements, including a navbar, footer, and individual knowledge cards. I have also designed pages for different content types, such as the homepage, category pages, and detailed content consumption, but my primary focus now is creating compelling Mongolian content. The mock content is where the rubber meets the road here, and it needs to be convincing.


**Translating Titles, Deepening Implementation**

I'm now generating realistic Mongolian titles for the knowledge cards, like "Тэнгэр яагаад цэнхэр байдаг вэ?" I'm also focusing on the low-level component implementation details. I'm exploring Tailwind color palettes and considering responsiveness with a mobile-first approach and a hamburger menu. The routing will use HashRouter. I'm also planning the content layout.


**Developing Detail Pages**

I'm now designing the detail page structure, with a placeholder video player (image with play button) at the top, followed by the content text. I've also planned a sidebar for related content. I'm deep into the coding phase, creating the fundamental files for the app. I will start by adding Google Fonts and defining types and constants. I will also make the layout wrapper, a sticky Navbar, knowledge card, and homepage.


**Implementing Specific Features**

I'm now zeroing in on UI details, like text colors and button styles.  Headings will use `text-slate-800`, body text `text-slate-600`, and primary buttons `bg-indigo-600`.  I'm also adding subtle hover effects to cards for a more engaging feel.  I'm making sure my imports and TypeScript interfaces are correct. All the text must be in Mongolian. I double-checked the XML format. I corrected my assumption to use HashRouter. I also confirmed good Cyrillic font support.


**Creating Core Files**

I've finalized the structure and generated the essential files: `metadata.json`, `index.html`, `index.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, and core components. I'm now polishing the Mongolian text, focusing on the critical pages. "About Us" is now "Бидний тухай", "Home" is "Нүүр", and "Search" is "Хайлт", and "Categories" is "Ангилал". I am also generating the `constants.ts` to reflect the specific categories provided, to ensure consistency. The next step is detailed implementation.

BRAND, LANGUAGE & VISUAL UPGRADE (ADD-ON PROMPT)

BRAND NAME (IMPORTANT)
- Official website name: "Channel Mongolia"
- Use this brand name consistently in:
  - Logo text
  - Header title
  - Page titles
  - Footer copyright text

LOGO & BRAND STYLE
- Logo type: Text-based wordmark
- Logo text: "Channel Mongolia"
- Font: Modern sans-serif, medium to semi-bold
- Slight letter spacing for a clean digital media feel

LOGO COLOR (MEDIUM DIGITAL BLUE)
- Update the logo color to a modern, medium digital blue.
- The blue should feel:
  - Professional
  - Trustworthy
  - Digital-media oriented
  - Calm and modern (NOT neon, NOT dark navy)

Recommended color direction:
- Primary logo blue: #2563EB or #1D4ED8
- Optional very subtle gradient: #2563EB → #3B82F6
- No strong glow effects.

LOGO INTERACTION
- Default: solid medium blue logo
- Hover:
  - Very subtle brightness increase
  - Slight soft shadow
  - Minimal scale increase (1–2%)

------------------------------------------------

BILINGUAL SUPPORT (CRITICAL)

- The website MUST support BOTH Mongolian and English UI.
- Default language: Mongolian (MN).
- Add a visible language switcher in the header: “MN | EN”.
- When language changes:
  - All menu items, buttons, titles, labels, and UI text switch instantly.

TRANSLATION STRUCTURE (INTERNAL)
- Use a simple key-value translation system.
- Mongolian translations are primary.
- English translations follow clean international wording.

Language examples:
- MN: "Нүүр" | EN: "Home"
- MN: "Ангилал" | EN: "Categories"
- MN: "Хайлт" | EN: "Search"
- MN: "Бидний тухай" | EN: "About"
- MN: "Сонирхолтой мэдлэгийг энгийнээр"
  EN: "Interesting knowledge, explained simply"

------------------------------------------------

OVERALL VISUAL TONE (2025 DIGITAL MEDIA STYLE)

- The website should feel like a modern digital knowledge channel.
- Calm, clean, professional — not flashy.
- Inspired by 2025 digital magazine & media platforms.

Design adjustments:
- Soft shadows instead of hard borders
- Clean card layouts with breathing space
- Minimal gradients, only where meaningful
- Slight glassmorphism for header (optional)
- Rounded corners: 12px consistency

COLOR PALETTE REFINEMENT
- Background: light gray or white
- Primary accent: medium digital blue (brand color)
- Secondary accent: muted teal or soft cyan
- Highlight accent (minimal use): soft orange

------------------------------------------------

HEADER STRUCTURE UPDATE

Header layout:
- Left: Logo ("Channel Mongolia")
- Center: Search bar
- Right: Language toggle (MN | EN)

Header behavior:
- Sticky on scroll
- Slight background blur
- Becomes more solid on scroll down

------------------------------------------------

CONTENT & TRUST SIGNALS

- Make spacing, typography, and hierarchy feel trustworthy.
- Content-first layout: text and thumbnails must feel readable and calm.
- No aggressive animations.
- Prepare natural places for future AdSense blocks without breaking UX.

------------------------------------------------

FINAL INTENT

"Channel Mongolia" should feel like:
- A modern Mongolian digital knowledge & media platform
- Trustworthy and professional
- Scalable for future growth (videos, podcasts, monetization)
- Calm, intelligent, and pleasant to explore

Do not overdesign.
Focus on clarity, balance, and long-term usability.

**Conceptualizing the Rebrand**

I'm now firmly focusing on rebranding "Meduun" to "Channel Mongolia" and incorporating bilingual support. Initial architecture discussions are favoring minimal disruption to the existing React with Tailwind CSS setup. I'm exploring the implications of the flat code structure in this context, especially as I consider localization strategies.


**Analyzing File Structures**

I've been examining the file structure and import patterns, specifically noting the implicit references to `components/` and `pages/` folders. Considering the provided file contents, I recognize the need to update these files to ensure consistency. I'm prioritizing the implementation of a `translations.ts` file or a `LanguageContext.tsx` to manage the bilingual support, favoring a React Context due to its straightforward key-value system for language switching throughout the app.


**Developing UI Translations**

I'm now implementing the UI translations, initially focusing on the Nav, buttons, headings, and static page text. While the prompt emphasizes instant switching of titles, which I interpret as UI elements, I'm considering whether to provide some English mock content. The mock articles may remain in Mongolian for now, as real content is DB-driven. I'm prioritizing the `constants.ts` and language integration.


**Focusing UI translations**

I'm now prioritizing the UI translations. While considering dynamic content, I am focusing on the user interface and static text, respecting the need for minimal updates. I've been establishing the `LanguageContext.tsx` to handle language state and translation functions, while also updating the `Navbar.tsx`, `Footer.tsx`, and `KnowledgeCard.tsx` for visual and text changes.  Additionally, I'm now working on translating static text in `Home.tsx` and UI buttons in `DetailPage.tsx`. The goal is to create a seamless bilingual experience.


**Expanding Translation Coverage**

I'm now expanding my focus to translate the remaining UI elements. Specifically, I'm updating `CategoriesPage.tsx`, `SearchPage.tsx`, and `AboutPage.tsx` to include translated headers, placeholders, and content. I'm also ensuring the `App.tsx` file is correctly wrapped with the LanguageProvider to ensure proper context. Additionally, I'm updating the `tailwind.config` to include the specific "Channel Mongolia" blue color and moving the search bar to the center on the desktop for layout improvements.


**Adding English Content**

I'm now adding English versions to mock content in `constants.ts` and updating relevant types in `types.ts` to accommodate the new fields for English titles, descriptions and categories. I'm also preparing to create a new `translations.ts` file to define a dictionary for UI elements and static text. Lastly, I'll be creating a `LanguageContext.tsx` file for the provider and hook to manage language switching. I am also updating the branding in `index.html` to reflect the new primary color requested.


**Restructuring Navigation**

I'm now restructuring the navigation, integrating the `useLanguage` hook and updating layouts to align with the revised header layout requirements. The current `Navbar` component is being reworked to position the logo on the left, the search bar in the center, and the language toggle on the right.  I'm exploring options for the navigation links, potentially placing them next to the logo or in a separate section. Based on the requirements, I am experimenting with different layouts, aiming for a clean and intuitive user experience that prioritizes search functionality and language accessibility.


I'm now implementing the navigation structure based on the revised design. The logo is positioned on the left, followed by the navigation links. The search bar, utilizing `flex-grow` for optimal width, sits centrally, while the language toggle and user login are on the right. I'm focusing on ensuring responsiveness for mobile views, and the planned structure includes a menu to replace the navigation links. I'm updating `Navbar.tsx` accordingly and reviewing the `tailwind.config` for layout constraints. I am updating `metadata.json`, `index.html`, `types.ts`, and `constants.ts` and will create `translations.ts` and `context/LanguageContext.tsx`.


**Organizing Translation Data**

I'm currently preparing the translation dictionary, focusing on UI elements and static text. I've compiled a list of necessary translations for the navigation, actions, headers, footer, metadata, and hero section. I'll utilize this data to create a `translations.ts` file or manage them from an existing one if possible, ensuring a well-organized and easily maintainable structure for the bilingual content.


**Adding Contextual Translations**

I'm now incorporating contextual translations into the `constants.ts` file, updating the `TRANSLATIONS` object, and adding English fields. I'm also ensuring that the types in `types.ts` accommodate the new language support. Additionally, I am focusing on refining the `App.tsx` file for provider wrapping, and updating `metadata.json` and `index.html` with the new project details. My current plan is to use a key-value translation approach, prioritizing a straightforward and easily manageable structure.


**Integrating Layout Components**

I'm now integrating the redesigned layout elements: `Navbar`, `Footer`, and `KnowledgeCard`. I've applied the Tailwind styles for the header layout.  I've wrapped the app with the language provider and am applying the context to all targeted components, making use of `constants.ts` and `translations.ts` where needed. The search bar is now centered and responsive, and language toggling is functional throughout the app, respecting the newly updated header specifications.


**Designing the Menu**

I'm now designing the menu, and have a few ideas to explore. I'm considering keeping links next to the logo on desktop, or creating a separate nav row if the search bar is too wide. The standard format of `[Logo] [Home] [Cat] [About] [Search] [Language] [User]` looks good. For the language toggle, I will use "MN | EN" buttons, with the active language in bold. I also started working on the visual tone, implementing `bg-slate-50` for the background and `bg-white shadow-sm hover:shadow-md border border-gray-100` for cards. payload.text:
ADVANCED SIDEBAR SYSTEM – MULTIPLE DISCOVERY BLOCKS (ADD-ON)

GENERAL SIDEBAR RULES
- Sidebar appears on the RIGHT side on desktop.
- Sticky behavior with top offset.
- On mobile:
  - Sidebar blocks move below main content
  - Or appear as collapsible sections.
- Sidebar design must match dark digital theme and remain calm, readable, and premium.

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 1: MOST VIEWED CONTENT

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Хамгийн их үзэлттэй мэдээлэл"

DESCRIPTION (INTERNAL):
- Shows top 5–10 contents based on view count.

Each item includes:
- Small thumbnail
- Title (1–2 lines)
- Meta:
  - "12,4K үзсэн"
  - "3 минут уншина"

Highlight:
- #1 item slightly larger
- Soft blue accent border

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 2: TRENDING TODAY

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Өнөөдрийн тренд"

DESCRIPTION:
- Content trending in the last 24 hours.
- Mark trending items visually.

Visual cue:
- 🔥 icon or soft orange indicator (very subtle)
- No aggressive color usage.

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 3: EDITOR'S PICK

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Редакторын онцлох"

DESCRIPTION:
- Curated articles selected manually.
- Quality over popularity.

Design:
- Card-style
- Slightly more spacing
- Calm accent border

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 4: DID YOU KNOW (MICRO FACTS)

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Та мэдэх үү?"

DESCRIPTION:
- Very short fun facts (1–2 sentences).
- No image required.

Design:
- Minimal card
- Quote-style layout
- Soft background contrast

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 5: QUICK CATEGORY JUMP

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Ангиллаар үзэх"

Categories (MONGOLIAN):
- Хүмүүс
- Дэлхий
- Түүх, газарзүй
- Шинжлэх ухаан
- Урлаг
- Спорт
- Монгол
- Амьтан, ургамал

Design:
- Pill-shaped buttons
- Blue border
- Glow on hover

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 6: LATEST UPDATES

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Сүүлд нэмэгдсэн"

DESCRIPTION:
- Shows newest 3–5 contents.
- Simple list format.

Meta:
- "1 цагийн өмнө"
- "Өчигдөр"

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 7: TIME-BASED FILTER

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Цаг хугацаагаар"

Options:
- "Сүүлийн 24 цаг"
- "Сүүлийн 7 хоног"
- "Сүүлийн 30 хоног"

Design:
- Toggle / pill style buttons
- Clear active state

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 8: READING TIME FILTER

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Унших хугацаа"

Options:
- "1–3 минут"
- "3–5 минут"
- "5+ минут"

Purpose:
- Helps users quickly choose content.

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 9: MOST SAVED / LIKED

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Хамгийн их хадгалсан"

DESCRIPTION:
- Sorted by saves or likes.
- Ideal for quality discovery.

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK 10: QUOTE / THOUGHT OF THE DAY

VISIBLE UI TITLE (MONGOLIAN):
- "Өнөөдрийн бодол"

DESCRIPTION:
- One inspirational or thought-provoking quote per day.
- Text-only.

Design:
- Elegant typography
- Centered text
- Very calm highlight

------------------------------------------------
BLOCK ORDER RECOMMENDATION (DESKTOP)

Suggested order:
1. Хамгийн их үзэлттэй мэдээлэл
2. Өнөөдрийн тренд
3. Редакторын онцлох
4. Та мэдэх үү?
5. Ангиллаар үзэх
6. Сүүлд нэмэгдсэн

------------------------------------------------
PERFORMANCE & UX NOTES

- Limit total visible blocks to avoid overload.
- Use lazy loading for sidebar blocks.
- Keep scrolling smooth and fast.

------------------------------------------------
FINAL INTENT

The sidebar system should:
- Encourage exploration
- Increase session time
- Guide users naturally
- Feel like part of the content, not advertising

Design must remain:
- Dark
- Digital
- Calm
- Professional
- Trustworthy

**Developing the Architecture**

I'm working on the initial architecture for the Advanced Sidebar System. The Channel Mongolia app's dark theme will guide the design. Right-side placement is confirmed. I'm focusing on creating discovery blocks within the sidebar.


**Designing Mobile Responsiveness**

I'm now thinking about how the sidebar will behave on mobile. I'm leaning towards a straightforward approach: below the main content, easily collapsible to maintain standard responsive design principles. It seems simpler than trying to force a sticky right-side element on smaller screens. I'm aiming for flexibility, initially incorporating all ten block options, while focusing on the recommended six for prominent display.


**Refining Sidebar Content**

I've been defining the content blocks for the sidebar.  I'm envisioning "Did You Know" facts in a quote style and a "Quick Category Jump" block with pill-shaped buttons for Mongolian categories. I'm also thinking about a "Latest Updates" list with time ago metadata, and then time/reading time filters, and a "Most Saved/Liked" block. Finally, there is the thought of a "Quote of the Day" block.


**Mapping the Implementation**

I've been solidifying the implementation strategy for the sidebar. I'm focusing on creating the `Sidebar.tsx` component as the central hub. I'm also preparing to update `constants.ts` with mock data for various blocks, including "Most Viewed," "Trending," and "Quotes."  I'm planning reusable sub-components like `SidebarBlock`, `ContentListBlock`, and specific components for each content type. Finally, I'll integrate this with `Home.tsx` and `DetailPage.tsx`, replacing the hardcoded sidebar sections with the new system.


**Prioritizing Implementation Steps**

I've been planning the implementation process meticulously. Right now, I'm concentrating on the visual design elements, ensuring the dark theme from the Channel Mongolia app is implemented. This involves defining backgrounds, borders, and glows, and text colors. I'm working to make sure the sidebar appears consistently on the right side on desktop. Next, I plan to move forward with the five key steps: updating `constants.ts`, creating `components/Sidebar.tsx`, updating `Home.tsx` and `DetailPage.tsx`, and ensuring proper styles. I will aim for a flexible sidebar block system, ready to receive block order recommendations in a later phase.


**Structuring Content Prioritization**

I'm now prioritizing the six core sidebar blocks: Trending, Editor's Pick, Did You Know, Category Jump, and Latest Updates, implementing them as the primary default configuration. The remaining blocks will still be developed as components, but I'll consider their initial rendering based on potential clutter and importance, placing less critical items lower in the sidebar. I'm focusing on defining the logic for these key components: Most Viewed, Trending (using an `isTrending` flag in `MOCK_CONTENT`), Editor's Pick (hardcoded IDs), Latest Updates (date-based sorting, potentially with time ago strings), Category Jump, and a Fact component leveraging existing facts. I'm updating `types.ts` to include `isTrending` and `isEditorPick` flags, and I'll modify `constants.ts` accordingly with mock content and translations. I'm also preparing the new `components/Sidebar.tsx` file for implementation.


**Finalizing the Integration**

I'm now integrating the sidebar within the existing pages. I'm focusing on updating `Home.tsx` and `DetailPage.tsx` to accommodate the new sidebar structure, ensuring a smooth transition. I've been considering grid layout adjustments for optimal visual flow, potentially exploring alternative configurations. I'm preparing to make `Most Viewed` #1 item distinct, and add a 🔥 icon for the `Trending` items. I'll utilize the `sticky top-20` class for the sidebar's position to work well with the navbar. The next step is adding keys for sidebar titles to `TRANSLATIONS` and adding `isTrending` and `isEditorPick` to `MOCK_CONTENT`. The `Sidebar.tsx` will need to consume and filter/sort the `MOCK_CONTENT`.

Based on your requirements for the **Advanced Sidebar System**, I will implement a comprehensive set of discovery blocks designed for the dark digital theme.

Here is the plan:
1.  **Update Data**: Add necessary flags (`isTrending`, `isEditorPick`) and translations for the new sidebar blocks.
2.  **Create Sidebar Component**: Build a modular `Sidebar.tsx` that implements the 6 recommended blocks (Most Viewed, Trending, Editor's Pick, Did You Know, Categories, Latest) plus the optional ones (Quotes, Filters) in a clean, sticky layout.
3.  **Integrate**: Replace the hardcoded sidebars in `Home.tsx` and `DetailPage.tsx` with this new system.

### Code Updates

payload.text:
You are a senior product designer, UX architect, and frontend web developer.

================================================
IMPORTANT LANGUAGE RULE
================================================
- All INTERNAL instructions, structure descriptions, and logic are in ENGLISH.
- ALL VISIBLE UI TEXT on the website (menus, buttons, titles, labels) MUST be in MONGOLIAN (Cyrillic).
- Use clean, modern, natural Mongolian language.
- Use a font that fully supports Mongolian Cyrillic.

================================================
BRAND IDENTITY
================================================
Brand name: "Channel Mongolia"

Brand feeling:
- Trustworthy digital media
- Modern knowledge platform
- Calm, intelligent, premium

Logo:
- Text-based logo: "Channel Mongolia"
- Medium digital blue color
- Clean, modern sans-serif
- Subtle hover glow (NOT neon)

================================================
PROJECT GOAL (INTERNAL – ENGLISH)
================================================
Build a modern informational & educational vlog website focused on:
- Interesting knowledge
- Curious & surprising facts
- Science
- History & geography
- Psychology & people
- Technology
- Nature & animals
- Mongolia-specific content

The website should feel:
- Premium
- Trustworthy
- Easy to read
- Addictive to explore

================================================
DESIGN STYLE – 2025 DIGITAL MEDIA
================================================
- Dark mode as PRIMARY
- Light mode as SECONDARY (day mode)
- Modern digital / tech-inspired
- Clean, calm, content-first
- Magazine + video hybrid layout
- Soft shadows, no harsh borders
- Rounded corners (12–16px)
- Glassmorphism (header only, subtle)
- Micro-interactions everywhere (hover, focus, scroll)

================================================
COLOR SYSTEM & CONTRAST (CRITICAL)
================================================

PRIMARY BRAND COLOR
- Medium digital blue (no neon)
- Used for:
  - Logo
  - Active navigation
  - Primary buttons
  - Key highlights

CONTRAST ACCENT COLORS
Use complementary contrast colors carefully:
- Cyan / Teal → secondary highlights
- Muted purple / indigo → section accents
- Soft warm orange → minimal emphasis only

------------------------------------------------
DARK MODE (DEFAULT)
------------------------------------------------
- Background: deep navy / charcoal with blue undertone
- Cards: slightly lighter dark surface
- Primary text: soft white
- Secondary text: muted blue-gray

------------------------------------------------
LIGHT MODE (DAY MODE)
------------------------------------------------
- Background: clean white or soft light-gray
- Cards: white with soft shadow
- Primary text: near-black
- Secondary text: dark gray

------------------------------------------------
COLOR RULES
------------------------------------------------
- Strong contrast for readability (WCAG-friendly)
- Never oversaturate
- Never use aggressive neon
- Accent colors should guide attention, not distract

================================================
DARK / LIGHT MODE TOGGLE
================================================
- Visible toggle in header
- Labels (VISIBLE UI – MONGOLIAN):
  - "Харанхуй горим"
  - "Өдрийн горим"
- Smooth animated transition
- No screen flash
- Brand color remains consistent in both modes

================================================
SITE NAVIGATION (VISIBLE UI – MONGOLIAN)
================================================
Main menu:
- "Нүүр"
- "Ангилал"
- "Хайлт"
- "Бидний тухай"

Header layout:
- Left: Logo ("Channel Mongolia")
- Center: Search bar
  - Placeholder: "Мэдлэг, баримт, түүх, технологи хайх..."
- Right:
  - MN / EN language toggle
  - Theme toggle

Header behavior:
- Sticky
- Semi-transparent
- Subtle blur
- Slight color change on scroll

================================================
CONTENT CATEGORIES (VISIBLE UI – MONGOLIAN)
================================================
- "Хүмүүс"
- "Дэлхий"
- "Түүх, газарзүй"
- "Шинжлэх ухаан"
- "Урлаг"
- "Спорт"
- "Монгол"
- "Амьтан, ургамал"

Categories appear as:
- Pill-shaped chips
- Category cards
- Filter options
- Sidebar quick links

================================================
HOME PAGE (KNOWLEDGE FEED)
================================================
HERO SECTION
- Main headline:
  "Сонирхолтой мэдлэгийг энгийнээр"
- Subtitle:
  "Өдөр бүр шинэ сонин хачин баримт, шинжлэх ухаан, түүхийн тайлбарууд"
- Background:
  - Very subtle animated gradient or noise
- Highlight one key word with accent color

CATEGORY CHIPS
- Horizontal scroll
- Glow on hover
- Active underline glow

------------------------------------------------
FEATURED CONTENT
------------------------------------------------
- Large featured card
- Image/video with soft vignette
- Title with 1 accented word
- Meta info:
  - 👁 "15,420 үзсэн"
  - ⏱ "5 минут"
  - 🏷 ангилал
- Minimal CTA:
  - "Унших" / "Үзэх"

------------------------------------------------
CONTENT GRID
------------------------------------------------
Cards include:
- Thumbnail
- Mongolian title
- Short description
- Category label
- Read time / views

Hover:
- Slight lift
- Soft blue glow
- Image zoom (very subtle)

================================================
SIDEBAR SYSTEM (DESKTOP)
================================================
Sticky right sidebar with these blocks:

1. "Хамгийн их үзэлттэй мэдээлэл"
2. "Өнөөдрийн тренд"
3. "Редакторын онцлох"
4. "Та мэдэх үү?"
5. "Сүүлд нэмэгдсэн"
6. "Ангиллаар үзэх"

Sidebar design:
- Dark surface
- Soft border
- Calm glow
- Never distracting

Mobile:
- Sidebar moves below content
- Or collapses into sections

================================================
CONTENT DETAIL PAGE
================================================
- Title (large, clear)
- Meta row:
  - "Нийтэлсэн огноо"
  - "Үзсэн тоо"
- Actions:
  - "Хадгалах"
  - "Хуваалцах"
  - "Таалагдлаа"
- Highlight boxes:
  - Title: "Сонирхолтой баримт"
- Section:
  - "Төстэй мэдлэгүүд"

================================================
MICRO-INTERACTIONS & MOTION
================================================
- Scroll reveal for sections
- Hover transitions (200–300ms)
- Button ripple glow
- Theme toggle fade animation

================================================
SEO & MONETIZATION READY
================================================
- Semantic HTML structure
- SEO-friendly headings
- Natural spaces for future AdSense
- Ads must not break reading flow

================================================
FINAL INTENT
================================================
Generate a premium 2025-style digital knowledge & media platform
named "Channel Mongolia" that:
- Uses dark/light modes professionally
- Has strong contrast and readability
- Feels modern, calm, and trustworthy
- Encourages long reading and exploration
- Looks premium on both desktop and mobile

Do NOT overdesign.
Focus on clarity, contrast, and long-term usability.

**Examining the Update**

I'm focusing now on the "Channel Mongolia" web app update. I'm prioritizing the dark/light mode toggle implementation. The initial hardcoding to dark mode is now being addressed.


**Prioritizing Visuals**

I've been working on the dark/light mode toggle. The primary colors are now implemented: Deep navy for dark mode and clean white/gray for light mode. I'm focusing on incorporating soft shadows, glassmorphism, and the "Medium digital blue" brand color across the interface. I'm also now ensuring the Theme Toggle and specific UI elements like the Hero text adhere to the provided guidelines, including Mongolian (Cyrillic) language support and English fallback.


**Defining Component States**

I'm now outlining a step-by-step plan. I'm focusing on implementing the theme context with localStorage for dark/light mode persistence and refining the Tailwind configuration, defining dark and light color variables. I'll need to update `index.html` to be controlled by React, and add the theme toggle to the Navbar.


**Finalizing Theme Integration**

I'm now fully integrating the theme across all components. Specifically, I'm updating `App.tsx` and wrapping with `ThemeProvider`. I'm then updating the Home, DetailPage, KnowledgeCard, and Sidebar components to ensure proper theme responsiveness. This involves meticulous updates to text styling, background colors, and component-specific styling like the "Interesting Fact" box. Also, I'm verifying proper theme support. Finally, I'm adding specific translations for "Dark Mode" and "Light Mode" within `constants.ts`.


**Incorporating UI/UX**

I'm now diving into the implementation details. I'm focusing on the Hero section with its animated gradient or noise requirement. I've updated the placeholder text in the Search Bar with the Mongolian translation. The ThemeContext is ready, and App.tsx and index.html are being integrated. I'm also preparing for the dual theme styles for components like KnowledgeCard, Sidebar, and FactBox. Finally, translations are being updated in `constants.ts` with Mongolian labels for the Theme toggle.


**Refining UI Text**

I'm now integrating the search placeholder "Мэдлэг, баримт, түүх, технологи хайх..." and the hero text "Сонирхолтой мэдлэгийг энгийнээр" and "Өдөр бүр шинэ сонин хачин баримт, шинжлэх ухаан, түүхийн тайлбарууд". I'm also revising the theme logic, aiming to prioritize localStorage over system preference for theme persistence and ensuring the `dark` class is applied to the `html` element on mount. Finally, I'm carefully updating the Tailwind config, specifically handling the background colors for light and dark modes. I'm focusing on defining dark and light modes through either CSS variables or direct Tailwind utility classes, to improve readability and to adhere with project standards.


**Optimizing Tailwind Classes**

I'm now revising my approach. I've decided to utilize standard Tailwind classes and specific hex values within the `tailwind.config` file, simplifying component styling and enhancing dark mode integration as requested. I'm focusing on updating `index.html` to remove the hardcoded background color, shifting control to Tailwind classes within `App.tsx` and the primary layout. I'm working with `@layer base`, and making sure colors are handled consistently.


**Implementing Direct Styles**

I'm now focusing on directly updating the `index.html` file to control the theme through CSS classes. I'm choosing to inline styles within a `style` tag in the `<head>`, specifically handling the `body` element's background and text colors. I'm now setting transition properties for smoother theme changes. The `html.dark` class is now used to trigger dark mode styles with specific hex values. For light mode, the `:not(.dark)` selector is being utilized, with `F8FAFC` and `0f172a` as the light mode background and text colors, respectively. I'm using the vanilla CSS approach.

Based on the detailed design specification for "Channel Mongolia," I have developed a set of changes to implement the Dark/Light mode toggle, refine the visual identity to the 2025 digital media style, and update the content structure.

### Key Changes
1.  **Theme System**: Added a `ThemeContext` and toggle functionality to switch between the premium Dark Mode (default) and the clean Light Mode.
2.  **Visual Overhaul**: Updated `index.html` styles and Tailwind configuration to support dynamic switching of backgrounds (`#0B1120` vs `#F8FAFC`) and surface colors.
3.  **Navbar & Header**: Added the theme toggle button, updated the search placeholder, and applied glassmorphism that works in both modes.
4.  **Content & Sidebar**: Refined `Sidebar`, `KnowledgeCard`, and `Home` components to use semantic color classes (`dark:bg-...` `bg-white`) ensuring legibility and aesthetic appeal in both themes.
5.  **Language & Copy**: Updated `constants.ts` with the specific Mongolian UI text requested (e.g., Search placeholder, Hero titles).

payload.text:
You are a senior product designer, UX architect, and frontend web developer.

================================================================
LANGUAGE RULE (CRITICAL)
================================================================
- All INTERNAL instructions, system logic, and design reasoning are in ENGLISH.
- ALL VISIBLE UI TEXT must be in MONGOLIAN (Cyrillic).
- Use clean, natural, modern Mongolian.
- Use a font that fully supports Mongolian Cyrillic.

================================================================
BRAND IDENTITY – CHANNEL MONGOLIA
================================================================
Brand name: Channel Mongolia

Brand personality:
- Premium digital media
- Knowledge-driven
- Calm, intelligent, modern
- Trustworthy and long-term

LOGO DESIGN (VERY IMPORTANT)
- Create a custom text-based logo:
  "Channel Mongolia"
- Use a modern geometric sans-serif font
- Logo weight: semi-bold
- Slight letter spacing for elegance

LOGO COLOR & STYLE:
- Logo uses a PREMIUM GRADIENT:
  Purple → Orange
- Example gradient direction:
  #6D28D9 (deep purple)
  →
  #F97316 (warm orange)

Rules:
- Gradient is smooth and soft (NOT neon)
- Logo looks premium in BOTH dark and light modes
- On hover:
  - Very subtle glow
  - Minimal brightness increase
- Logo must feel unique and brand-defining

================================================================
PROJECT GOAL (INTERNAL – ENGLISH)
================================================================
Build a modern 2025 informational & educational digital media platform
focused on:
- Interesting knowledge
- Curious facts
- Science
- History & geography
- Technology
- Psychology & people
- Nature & animals
- Mongolia-focused content

The site should feel:
- Premium
- Editorial
- Calm but engaging
- Addictive to explore
- Easy to read for long sessions

================================================================
DESIGN STYLE – 2025 PREMIUM DIGITAL MEDIA
================================================================
- Dark mode = DEFAULT
- Light mode = Day mode
- Editorial + streaming hybrid
- Content-first
- Soft depth, no harsh borders
- Rounded corners (14–16px)
- Subtle glassmorphism (header only)
- Smooth micro-animations
- Professional, not flashy

================================================================
COLOR SYSTEM – PURPLE & ORANGE (CORE)
================================================================

PRIMARY BRAND GRADIENT (KEY IDENTITY)
- Gradient: Purple → Orange
- Used for:
  - Logo
  - Hero keyword highlight
  - CTA buttons
  - Active states
  - Badges (TOP / TREND)

SECONDARY SUPPORT COLORS
- Indigo / soft violet for structure
- Muted cyan for secondary actions
- Warm orange ONLY for emphasis

------------------------------------------------
DARK MODE (DEFAULT)
------------------------------------------------
- Background: very dark purple-blue / charcoal
- Cards: slightly lighter surface
- Primary text: soft white
- Secondary text: muted lavender-gray

------------------------------------------------
LIGHT MODE (DAY MODE)
------------------------------------------------
- Background: soft off-white
- Cards: white with light shadow
- Primary text: near-black
- Secondary text: neutral gray

------------------------------------------------
COLOR RULES
------------------------------------------------
- Purple = Brand depth
- Orange = Attention & warmth
- White = Readability
- Never oversaturate
- Never use harsh neon

================================================================
DARK / LIGHT MODE TOGGLE
================================================================
- Visible toggle in header
- Labels (VISIBLE UI):
  - "Харанхуй горим"
  - "Өдрийн горим"
- Smooth fade transition
- Zero flicker
- Colors adapt slightly per mode

================================================================
HEADER & NAVIGATION (VISIBLE UI – MONGOLIAN)
================================================================
Menu:
- Нүүр
- Ангилал
- Хайлт
- Бидний тухай

Header layout:
- Left: Gradient logo (Channel Mongolia)
- Center: Search bar
  Placeholder:
  "Мэдлэг, баримт, түүх, технологи хайх..."
- Right:
  - MN | EN language toggle
  - Dark / Light toggle
  - "Нэвтрэх"

Header behavior:
- Sticky
- Blur background
- Subtle color shift on scroll

================================================================
CONTENT CATEGORIES
================================================================
- Хүмүүс
- Дэлхий
- Түүх, газарзүй
- Шинжлэх ухаан
- Урлаг
- Спорт
- Монгол
- Амьтан, ургамал

Displayed as:
- Gradient-accent pill chips
- Category cards
- Sidebar navigation

================================================================
HOME PAGE – HERO
================================================================
Headline:
"Сонирхолтой мэдлэгийг **энгийнээр**"

- Highlight the word “энгийнээр” using
  purple → orange gradient text.

Subtitle:
"Өдөр бүр шинэ сонин хачин баримт, шинжлэх ухаан, түүхийн тайлбарууд"

Background:
- Very subtle animated gradient/noise
- Extremely slow movement (almost invisible)

================================================================
FEATURED CONTENT (ОНЦЛОХ МЭДЛЭГ)
================================================================
- Large hero card
- Image/video with vignette
- Title with one gradient-highlighted word
- Meta row:
  👁 15,420 үзсэн
  ⏱ 5 минут
  🏷 Ангилал

CTA:
- Gradient outline button:
  "Унших" / "Үзэх"

================================================================
CONTENT GRID
================================================================
Cards include:
- Image
- Title
- Short description
- Category
- Meta info

Hover:
- Soft lift
- Image zoom (1.03)
- Gradient border reveal (purple → orange)

================================================================
SIDEBAR SYSTEM (DESKTOP)
================================================================
Sticky sidebar blocks:

1. Хамгийн их үзэлттэй мэдээлэл
2. Өнөөдрийн тренд
3. Редакторын онцлох
4. Та мэдэх үү?
5. Сүүлд нэмэгдсэн
6. Ангиллаар үзэх

Rules:
- #1 item marked with gradient “TOP” badge
- Calm, readable, helpful
- Never distracting

Mobile:
- Sidebar collapses or moves below content

================================================================
CONTENT DETAIL PAGE
================================================================
- Big clear title
- Meta:
  Нийтэлсэн огноо
  Үзсэн тоо
- Actions:
  Хадгалах
  Хуваалцах
  Таалагдлаа
- Highlight box:
  "Сонирхолтой баримт"
- Related:
  "Төстэй мэдлэгүүд"

================================================================
MOTION & MICRO-INTERACTIONS
================================================================
- Scroll reveal
- Hover transitions (200ms)
- Button glow ripple
- Theme toggle fade

================================================================
SEO & MONETIZATION READY
================================================================
- Semantic HTML
- Clean heading hierarchy
- Natural AdSense placement (future)
- User trust first

================================================================
FINAL RESULT
================================================================
Generate a 100% premium, production-ready,
2025-level digital knowledge platform named:

"Channel Mongolia"

The site must:
- Look unmistakably premium
- Use purple–orange gradient elegantly
- Have perfect contrast & readability
- Feel calm, modern, and editorial
- Work beautifully on desktop & mobile

Do NOT overdesign.
Focus on balance, clarity, and timeless quality.

**Envisioning the Redesign**

I'm now fully immersed in the redesign of "Channel Mongolia". I've established core language requirements: English for internal instructions, and Mongolian (Cyrillic) for the visible user interface. I'm focusing on "Premium 2025 Digital Media" aesthetics and function as the guiding principle.


**Developing the Brand**

I've got the basics for the brand sorted. "Channel Mongolia" it is! I'm leaning towards a geometric sans-serif logo with a premium gradient, purple to orange. The goal is a calm, knowledge-driven, and modern aesthetic. I've also nailed down the color system: dark mode with deep purple-blue, light mode with off-white, and strategic accent colors. Next up are the layout and UI elements.


**Implementing UI Elements**

My current focus is on the specific UI elements. I'm visualizing pill chips with gradient accents throughout the design. For the hero section, the headline "Сонирхолтой мэдлэгийг **энгийнээр**" will be emphasized with a gradient on "энгийнээр."  I'm also working on featured content cards with gradient outline CTAs, content grid cards that enhance with hover effects, and a sticky sidebar with prominent "TOP" badges. Finally, I'm working to make dark/light mode work even better.


**Addressing UI Implementation**

I'm now diving into the implementation details. I've confirmed all Mongolian text constants are correct and updated them where needed. The navbar is now structured as specified, with gradient text applied to the logo and navigation links updated. The sidebar's "TOP" badge uses a gradient, and headers are styled to be calming and premium. I'm also implementing the hover effect with gradient borders and visual lift and zoom on the KnowledgeCard. For the homepage, the hero section has the gradient on "энгийнээр," and category chips employ gradient styles on hover and active states. No major changes were made to types.ts.


**Building Global Foundations**

I'm now focused on the global styling with Tailwind. I've updated the `index.html` to establish the color palette, including `brand-purple`, `brand-orange`, and the `dark-bg` color. I'm using the violet and orange palettes, but I've specifically defined the brand gradient colors. I've updated the `body` styles to apply the `dark-bg` for dark mode. Now, I'm integrating these styles into the `Navbar`, `Home`, and `KnowledgeCard` components.


**Addressing Component Details**

I'm now focusing on specific component implementations. The hover effect for the `KnowledgeCard` will utilize a subtle shadow with a color shift to orange/purple. The `Sidebar` component will incorporate the badge logic. I've verified the translations in `constants.ts`, and the dark background color will remain deep navy/charcoal with a blue undertone. The light background will stick with `#F8FAFC`. I'm confirming that the logo font, Roboto, will maintain the weight and tracking as planned. I'll review text requirements for the menu.


**Structuring for Launch**

I'm now detailing the component implementations required for launch. The updated `constants.ts` accurately reflects the exact wording for key elements. I've updated the `Navbar` component, adding the gradient logo and re-evaluating the menu structure, prioritizing search functionality. For the `Home` section, I've integrated the gradient text highlight for the hero headline and am updating the visual style for the category pills. Lastly, the `KnowledgeCard` will have a refined hover effect to reinforce the premium branding and the `Sidebar` will be implemented.


**Adding Footer & Refinement**

Okay, I've got the new Footer component implemented, and the logo is updated there as well. The types remain unchanged. I'm now refining the "Gradient Border Reveal" effect for the cards using the described technique, creating that dynamic border that really pops.

To implement the premium "Channel Mongolia" brand identity with the Purple-Orange gradient system and modern 2025 digital media aesthetic, I will update the core styling configuration, constants, and key components.

Here are the changes:

1.  **Style Configuration (`index.html`)**: Defines the specific Purple (`#6D28D9`) and Orange (`#F97316`) brand colors and updates the dark mode background to a deep charcoal-purple tone.
2.  **Constants (`constants.ts`)**: Updates all UI text to the specific Mongolian copy requested, including the Hero headline structure.
3.  **Navbar (`Navbar.tsx`)**: Implements the gradient text logo ("Channel Mongolia"), centers the search bar, and refines the premium glassmorphism look.
4.  **Home Page (`Home.tsx`)**: Updates the Hero section to highlight "энгийнээр" with the brand gradient and applies the new category chip styling.
5.  **Cards (`KnowledgeCard.tsx`)**: Adds the "Gradient Border Reveal" effect on hover using a wrapper technique.
6.  **Sidebar (`Sidebar.tsx`)**: Adds the "TOP" badge with gradient background for the #1 ranked item.
7.  **Footer (`Footer.tsx`)**: Updates branding to match the new identity.

================================================
MAIN NAVIGATION ORDER & BACKGROUND DESIGN (ADD-ON)
================================================

NAVIGATION CATEGORY ORDER (CRITICAL)

Set the main content categories in the following EXACT order
across all places where categories are shown
(header menus, dropdowns, sidebar, filters):

1. "Монгол"
2. "Дэлхий"
3. "Хүмүүс"
4. "Шинжлэх ухаан"
5. "Түүх, газарзүй"
6. "Урлаг"
7. "Спорт"
8. "Амьтан, ургамал"

This order must be:
- Consistent everywhere
- Never shuffled or auto-sorted
- Treated as the primary editorial hierarchy

------------------------------------------------
HEADER NAVIGATION STRUCTURE (VISIBLE UI – MONGOLIAN)
------------------------------------------------

Top navigation layout:

- Logo: "Channel Mongolia" (purple → orange gradient)
- Main menu items:
  - "Нүүр"
  - "Монгол"
  - "Дэлхий"
  - "Хүмүүс"
  - "Шинжлэх ухаан"

  - "Урлаг"
  - "Спорт"
  - "Амьтан, ургамал"
  - "Видео"
- Utility items (right side):
  - Search
  - MN | EN language toggle
  - Dark / Light mode toggle

If screen width is limited:
- Group categories under "Ангилал" dropdown
- Keep the SAME order inside the dropdown

------------------------------------------------
NAVIGATION BACKGROUND & VISUAL STYLE
------------------------------------------------

Navigation background:
- Dark digital surface
- Subtle purple–blue gradient
- Semi-transparent with blur (glassmorphism)

Example visual feel:
- Dark violet → deep indigo
- Very soft gradient (almost invisible)
- No hard lines

------------------------------------------------
MENU ITEM STYLING
------------------------------------------------

Default state:
- Text color: soft white / muted lavender
- Clean spacing
- Medium font weight

Hover state:
- Text shifts to gradient accent (purple → orange)
- Soft underline glow
- Very smooth transition (200ms)

Active state:
- Gradient underline
- Slight text brightness increase
- Subtle glow below the item

------------------------------------------------
MOBILE NAVIGATION
------------------------------------------------

Mobile menu:
- Full-height drawer or slide-down panel
- Same category order as desktop
- Larger touch targets
- Clear separation between items

Background:
- Dark purple digital surface
- Slight gradient depth
- Comfortable spacing

------------------------------------------------
VISUAL CONSISTENCY RULES
------------------------------------------------

- Navigation must feel calm, premium, and authoritative
- Do NOT overcrowd
- Do NOT use neon or loud effects
- Background supports readability
- Categories feel like editorial sections, not buttons

------------------------------------------------
FINAL INTENT
------------------------------------------------

The navigation system should:
- Clearly communicate content structure
- Feel balanced and professional
- Highlight the importance of Mongolian content first
- Match the purple–orange premium brand identity
- Work beautifully on desktop and mobile

**Rearranging the Categories**

I'm currently working on updating the main navigation for "Channel Mongolia".  The priority is to change the category order. "Монгол" will now be first, followed by "Дэлхий", and then "..." I'm exploring the design implications of this rearrangement and its impact on user flow. The new order is the primary focus.


**Adding New Categories**

I've incorporated "Хүмүүс," "Шинжлэх ухаан," "Түүх, газарзүй," "Урлаг," "Спорт," and "Амьтан, ургамал" into the main navigation. "Видео" is considered for inclusion as well. I'm evaluating how to integrate these, especially under limited screen space, which might lead to an "Ангилал" dropdown. The updated layout will feature the logo, main menu, and utility items (Search, Language, Theme).


**Adjusting the Utility Items**

I'm now revising the utility items on the right side of the header. I'm prioritizing the order of Search, Language toggle (MN | EN), and Dark/Light mode, as instructed. I'll include "Login" if space allows, but it's secondary. Considering the design, I'm sticking to the most recent prompt regarding the *Main Navigation Order* but I generally want to keep it functional.


**Visualizing the Menu**

I'm now focusing on the visual aspects of the navigation. A full-height drawer is the chosen method, mirroring the category order previously established. I'm opting for a dark purple digital surface background. The structure, especially on desktop, aims for efficient use of available space. I'll utilize a responsive design strategy to accommodate different screen sizes, with the goal of showcasing all menu items in a horizontal list on XL screens, potentially employing an intelligent grouping.


**Refining Navigation Placement**

I'm now grappling with the discrepancy between the header layout and the main menu items. The prompt's instructions conflict: does the search bar occupy the center, leaving no room for the categories? I'm now exploring common media site patterns to resolve this, considering a two-row approach or incorporating search as an icon. The goal is to provide easy access to categories while maintaining the search function. I'm focusing on the positioning and prioritising of the main elements within the layout.


**Analyzing Layout Constraints**

I'm now back at the header layout and the placement of the main menu items. It seems the instructions conflict: centering the search bar leaves no room for the navigation links. I'm exploring solutions like a two-row header, or integrating the search bar as an icon. I'm taking another look at the original prompt requirements, specifically the "Header layout" description, to see if the navigation can still be included directly. The aim is to prioritize easy category access while maintaining a prominent search function. I'm also considering adapting a more common layout, incorporating a top bar for utilities and a secondary bar for navigation, if necessary. I'm looking for a way to satisfy both requirements without creating a confusing layout.


**Designing the Navigation Structure**

I'm now determining the most effective placement of the main menu items, which include Mongolia and World categories, given the constraints. Since the centered search bar might not leave space, I'm now exploring whether to adopt a double-navbar approach or a single, more compact navbar. I'm prioritizing direct category visibility and easy search access.


**Evaluating Layout Feasibility**

I'm now determining the most effective placement of the main menu items, which include Mongolia and World categories, given the constraints.  The two-row header might be the optimal approach. I'm exploring the feasibility of a single row, and considering the implications of a compact search bar or smaller text. I'll stick to the core prompt and try to include as many visible categories as possible.


**Implementing the Layout**

I've decided on the two-row header, with the logo and search bar centered on the top row, and navigation items below. This seems to be the most viable way to accommodate all requirements without sacrificing accessibility or design. The background will be the "dark digital surface" with a subtle purple-blue gradient, as specified. Now, I'm working to make the visual effects and file changes. I'll focus on the specific background, hover effects, and ensure that the order of the categories are correct, adding video.


**Adjusting Header Layout**

I'm now revising my decision on the header layout. The two-row approach seems the most logical, even after reconsidering the prompt's wording on the search bar's center alignment. Modern designs like The Verge show that it's possible to include the search function with the categories to preserve vertical space. Therefore, I will implement a two-row header to balance the "Visible Search Bar" and "Visible Menu Items" requirements, which is the only logical solution.


**Updating Code Implementation**

I've reordered the `CATEGORIES` constant and integrated "Video" as a dedicated nav link. The structural setup now includes a sticky header with a top bar (logo, search, actions) and a navigation bar (home, categories). Adapting the design, the sidebar and mobile menus also reflect the updated category order. I'm focusing on language translations for newly added items to ensure consistency across the application.


**Finalizing Navigation Elements**

I'm currently finalizing the navigation by implementing the "Video" category.  The "Video" requirement is implemented as a dedicated link in `Navbar.tsx`, so it's ready. The design considerations like the dark digital surface background with a subtle purple-blue gradient are also integrated. All related files are checked for consistency and are ready for testing.


**Refactoring Navigation Elements**

I'm now refactoring the `constants.ts` file to ensure the category order is precise and reflects the updated priorities, and the navbar (`Navbar.tsx`) has had the "video" item added. I'm focusing on the implementation of the main navigation and considering the `activeCategory` logic used within `Home.tsx` in `CategoriesPage`. I'm verifying the consistency across all components.

Based on your instructions, I will redesign the navigation system to prioritize the specific category order and implement the premium two-row header layout (on desktop) to accommodate the Search Bar, Logo, and full Category list without clutter.

Here are the specific changes:
1.  **`constants.ts`**: Reordering the `CATEGORIES` array to match the exact editorial hierarchy (Mongolia first) and adding "Video" translation keys.
2.  **`components/Navbar.tsx`**: Implementing a **Premium Double-Row Header**:
    *   **Top Row**: Logo, Centered Search Bar, Utilities (Language, Theme, Login).
    *   **Bottom Row**: Horizontal Navigation Menu with the specific category order.
    *   **Styling**: Applied the dark digital surface with subtle purple-blue gradient and glassmorphism.
3.  **`Sidebar.tsx`**: Ensuring the sidebar block "Browse Categories" reflects the new sorting order automatically via the constants update.

payload.text:
You are the official AI assistant of the website “Channel Mongolia”.

================================================================
LANGUAGE & COMMUNICATION RULES (CRITICAL)
================================================================
- You MUST respond ONLY in Mongolian (Cyrillic).
- Use friendly, polite, and natural Mongolian language.
- Keep responses short and clear.
- Ask only ONE question at a time.
- Never pressure the user to answer.

================================================================
ROLE & PURPOSE
================================================================
You have three core roles:

1. Help users explore content and categories.
2. Collect feedback about content quality and user interests.
3. Understand what users like, dislike, and want to see more of.

You are a feedback-oriented assistant, not just an information bot.

================================================================
WEBSITE STRUCTURE (FOR CONTEXT)
================================================================
Main sections:
- Монгол
- Дэлхий
- Хүмүүс
- Шинжлэх ухаан
- Түүх, газарзүй
- Урлаг
- Спорт
- Амьтан, ургамал
- Видео
- Бидний тухай
- Нууцлалын бодлого
- Үйлчилгээний нөхцөл

================================================================
CONTENT RATING BEHAVIOR
================================================================

After a user reads, watches, or asks about content,
politely ask for feedback.

Use questions like:

- “Энэ контент танд хэр таалагдав?”
Options:
- ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Маш их таалагдсан)
- ⭐⭐⭐⭐
- ⭐⭐⭐
- ⭐⭐
- ⭐ (Таалагдаагүй)

If the user gives a rating:
- Thank them politely.
- Do NOT ask multiple follow-ups immediately.

================================================================
CONTENT PREFERENCE SURVEY
================================================================

Occasionally (not always), ask one of the following:

- “Та ямар төрлийн контент илүү сонирхож байна вэ?”
Options (present as simple list):
- Монгол
- Дэлхий
- Хүмүүс
- Шинжлэх ухаан
- Түүх, газарзүй
- Урлаг
- Спорт
- Амьтан, ургамал
- Видео

OR

- “Танд ямар төрлийн контент илүү таалагдсан бэ?”
- “Цаашдаа ямар сэдвийн талаар их үзмээр байна вэ?”

Rules:
- Never ask more than one survey question at a time.
- If the user declines, respect it and continue normally.

================================================================
LIKE / DISLIKE SIGNALS
================================================================

If the user says something like:
- “Таалагдлаа”
- “Сонирхолтой байна”
- “Дахин иймэрхүү юм үзмээр байна”

You should:
- Acknowledge positively.
- Suggest a related category or video.

If the user says:
- “Таалагдсангүй”
- “Урт байна”
- “Сонирхолгүй”

You should:
- Respect the feedback.
- Ask gently:
  “Ямар төрлийн контент илүү таалагдах байсан гэж бодож байна вэ?”

================================================================
SMART RECOMMENDATIONS
================================================================

Based on user feedback:
- Recommend similar content types.
- Example:
  “Та ‘Монгол’ ангиллын контент сонирхож байгаа бол манай сайтад холбогдох нийтлэл, видеонууд бий.”

Do NOT invent exact article titles.
Refer only to categories or sections.

================================================================
WELCOME MESSAGE (FIRST MESSAGE)
================================================================

When the chat opens, say:

“Сайн байна уу 👋  
Channel Mongolia сайтад тавтай морилно уу.  

Та манай контентоос юу илүү сонирхож байгаагаа хуваалцвал
бид илүү тохирсон мэдлэг, видеог санал болгох болно.”

================================================================
ETHICS & SAFETY
================================================================
- Do NOT collect personal data.
- Do NOT ask for name, phone, or email.
- Feedback is anonymous.
- Be respectful and neutral at all times.

================================================================
FINAL INTENT
================================================================
Your goal is to help improve Channel Mongolia
by understanding what content users enjoy the most,
while keeping the experience friendly, optional, and respectful.

**Envisioning AI Assistant**

I've been mapping out the initial design for the Channel Mongolia AI assistant. The focus is now on ensuring it can flawlessly guide users through the site's content and categories, all while maintaining a strictly Mongolian language interface.  I'm also considering potential future features, like perhaps summarizing video content.


**Analyzing User Interactions**

I'm now deep-diving into the user interaction aspect. My focus is on crafting a welcoming and engaging experience. I'm prioritizing polite and natural Mongolian responses, keeping replies concise and clear, and structuring the conversation with one question at a time. I'm also planning to implement content rating prompts and preference surveys to gather valuable feedback. Furthermore, the AI assistant will offer smart recommendations based on browsing categories. Crucially, I'm adhering to strict constraints: no personal data collection or generating fake article titles. All of this will be implemented using the Gemini API, of course.


**Designing UI Components**

I'm now focused on the UI, specifically the `ChatAssistant` component. I'm ensuring it's available site-wide. I'll need to style it to match Channel Mongolia's brand, using purple and orange, and incorporating glassmorphism effects for visual appeal. I'm also carefully planning how I'll handle the API key securely. I'm going to start with `process.env.API_KEY` as instructed. I'm leveraging React hooks to manage the component's state, and I will instantiate the `GoogleGenAI` instance.

**Defining Welcome Flow**

I'm now focusing on the initial interaction with users. I'll load the welcome message directly into the `messages` state. The system will use `gemini-2.5-flash` for a balance of speed and functionality. The user interface will include a button, a message window with scrollable chat history, and a text input field, along with a send button for user input. For the UI, the button will be bottom-right fixed with rounded corners. I also will handle the API key by directly using `process.env.API_KEY` for initialization. Finally, I will strictly adhere to including the content in the `systemInstruction` prompt directly. I am also investigating structured output for better user feedback, possibly rendering as buttons, even though the prompt suggests the AI asks.


**Implementing Feedback Mechanisms**

I'm now zeroing in on gathering user feedback. After reflecting on the "UX Architect" comment, I've decided against complex custom rating widgets for the initial implementation. The design will use simple text-based options for user ratings, as the prompt specifies, and this offers a fast, dependable user experience. While quick reply chips could elevate the experience later, I will start with a basic chat interface where the AI *suggests* options. I've also locked down the prompt for the "systemInstruction" prompt. I have created the `ChatAssistant.tsx` file and included it in the `App.tsx` file.


**Optimizing Conversation Flow**

I'm now thinking through how to manage the conversation flow and API interaction.  I'm exploring the nuances of state management within the `ChatAssistant` component. While the SDK offers chat history management, I'm leaning toward a stateless approach using `ai.chats.create` with the full history each time, for reliability and easier integration with React. I need to be sure the API key is passed correctly, as per the initial implementation with `process.env.API_KEY`, but I'm thinking of how to better separate API interaction and component state.


**Refining Code Implementation**

I'm now implementing the `ChatAssistant.tsx` file, focusing on the core logic and structure. I'm prioritizing the `messages` state in React, as the central source of truth for the conversation history. I'll pass the `history` to `ai.chats.create` with stateless approach to `ai.chat.sendMessage(currentInput)` whenever the user sends a message. I'm including the prompt content inside the `systemInstructions`, including Language and Role and Purpose.


**Integrating API Interaction**

I'm now integrating the Gemini API directly into the `ChatAssistant` component. I've successfully mapped the React state `messages` into the `Content[]` format required by `chats.create`. I'm using `import.meta.env.VITE_API_KEY` for the API key, as it's the standard practice in my development environment. The welcome message is now pre-populated in both the UI state and the model history, simulating the AI's initial greeting. I've also added the `ChatAssistant` component to the `App.tsx` file to ensure the chat interface is rendered on the page. I'm focusing on ensuring the API calls are efficient and the state management is robust.


**Constructing UI Layout**

I'm now fully immersed in the design details of the chat interface, following the provided specifications meticulously. I'm focusing on the fixed position and dimensions of the container, ensuring it maintains its size. I've successfully implemented the gradient header and messages, and I'm using the scrollable messages area. I'm also now focusing on the bottom input field.

To implement the Channel Mongolia AI Assistant, I will create a new component `ChatAssistant.tsx` that integrates with the Google GenAI SDK. This component will handle the chat interface, message history, and interaction with the `gemini-2.5-flash` model using the specific Mongolian system instructions provided.

I will then update `App.tsx` to include this assistant globally.

### Design Specification

1.  **Visual Style**:
    *   **Floating Action Button (FAB)**: Located at the bottom-right, using the brand's purple-orange gradient.
    *   **Chat Window**: A glassmorphism-styled panel (glass effect matching the Navbar) appearing above the FAB.
    *   **Message Bubbles**:
        *   **AI**: Gray/Dark surface background with text.
        *   **User**: Brand gradient background with white text.
    *   **Typography**: Consistent with the site's `Inter`/`Roboto` fonts.

2.  **Behavior**:
    *   **Initialization**: Displays the specific Welcome Message immediately upon opening.
    *   **Context**: Maintains conversation history.
    *   **System Instruction**: Strictly enforces the Mongolian language, role, and feedback collection rules defined in the prompt.
    *   **Loading State**: Shows a typing indicator while fetching responses.

3.  **Tech Stack**:
    *   `@google/genai` for the API client.
    *   React state for message management.
    *   `lucide-react` for icons.

payload.text:
You are the official AI system designer, UX architect, and assistant
for the website “Channel Mongolia”.

================================================================
LANGUAGE RULE (CRITICAL)
================================================================
- ALL visible UI text and chatbot responses MUST be in Mongolian (Cyrillic).
- Language must be clean, simple, friendly, and natural.
- Internal logic and behavior are in English.

================================================================
CORE GOAL
================================================================
Transform Channel Mongolia from a passive knowledge website into
an interactive, personalized, and habit-forming digital media platform.

The system must:
- Understand user interests
- Encourage daily visits
- Turn readers into active participants
- Improve learning retention

================================================================
FEATURE 1: PERSONALIZED CONTENT FEED
================================================================

GOAL (INTERNAL)
Provide each user with content tailored to their interests and behavior.

LOGIC:
- Track (conceptually):
  - Categories the user reads or watches
  - Content the user rates positively
  - Topics the user asks the chatbot about
  - Preference for video or text

VISIBLE UI (MONGOLIAN):
Section title:
- "Танд санал болгох мэдлэг"

Description:
- "Таны сонирхолд тулгуурласан контент"

BEHAVIOR:
- Personalized content appears first on the Home page.
- Other content remains visible.
- If insufficient data exists, show a balanced mix of popular content.

CHATBOT ROLE:
- Occasionally asks:
  “Та ямар төрлийн контент илүү сонирхож байна вэ?”
- Uses answers to refine recommendations.

USER EXPERIENCE RULE:
- Personalization must feel helpful, not invasive.

================================================================
FEATURE 2: DAILY KNOWLEDGE – “ӨНӨӨДРИЙН МЭДЛЭГ”
================================================================

GOAL (INTERNAL)
Create a daily habit by offering one short, interesting fact each day.

VISIBLE UI (MONGOLIAN):
Section title:
- "Өнөөдрийн мэдлэг"

FORMAT:
- One short fact
- Under 30 seconds reading time
- Surprising but easy to understand

PLACEMENT:
- Home page (top)
- Sidebar (desktop)
- Card format on mobile

INTERACTION:
Below the fact, show:
- “Энэ танд сонирхолтой байв уу?”

Options:
- 👍 Таалагдсан
- 👎 Таалагдаагүй

CHATBOT RESPONSE:
- Politely thank the user
- Adjust future suggestions based on feedback

RULES:
- Only one daily item
- No overload
- Easy to share

================================================================
FEATURE 3: INTERACTIVE QUIZ – “ХАРИУ НЬ ЮУ ВЭ?”
================================================================

GOAL (INTERNAL)
Turn passive reading into active learning.

VISIBLE UI (MONGOLIAN):
Card title:
- "Хариу нь юу вэ?"

FORMAT:
- Short question related to the content
- Answer hidden by default
- Reveals on click with smooth animation

OPTIONAL:
- Multiple choice (2 options)
- Immediate friendly feedback

PLACEMENT:
- Middle or end of articles
- Used sparingly

CHATBOT FOLLOW-UP:
- Asks:
  “Энэ төрлийн асуулт танд таалагдлаа юу?”
- If yes, suggests similar content

RULES:
- Fun, not exam-like
- No scoring pressure
- No negative feedback

================================================================
CHATBOT INTEGRATION (GLOBAL)
================================================================

The chatbot must:
- Help users navigate the site
- Recommend content
- Collect feedback (ratings, interests)
- Improve personalization over time

Behavior rules:
- Ask only ONE question at a time
- Never force feedback
- Respect user choices

================================================================
ETHICS & SAFETY
================================================================
- No personal data collection
- Feedback is anonymous
- If unsure, say so clearly
- Do not hallucinate specific article titles

================================================================
FINAL INTENT
================================================================
Channel Mongolia should feel like:
- A smart knowledge companion
- A place users return to daily
- A platform that learns from its audience

The experience must be:
- Calm
- Respectful
- Intelligent
- Engaging

**Crafting a Plan**

I'm focusing on "Channel Mongolia," aiming to elevate it from a basic website to an engaging platform. The plan involves three key features for personalization and interaction, designed to foster regular engagement. I'm thinking about how each feature will integrate and contribute to habit formation, going beyond simple utility.


**Defining UI and Logic**

I've got the UI requirements down for the personalized feed, including the Mongolian title "Танд санал болгох мэдлэг". Now I'm grappling with the recommendation logic. Simulating it with local storage or React Context seems feasible, given the absence of a backend. Also, I've got a framework for the "Өнөөдрийн мэдлэг" daily fact feature, which will appear on both the Home page and Sidebar. The design of the feature includes a simple interaction prompt, using thumbs up and thumbs down buttons. The Mongolian UI and chatbot language are a must-have for the whole project.


**Considering Connections**

I'm working on connecting the "Өнөөдрийн мэдлэг" daily fact with the chatbot to get real-time feedback, or to handle it separately for now. I've designed the UI for an interactive quiz, "Хариу нь юу вэ?", a short question with a hidden answer revealed on click. It will be integrated into articles. I'm also preparing for the chatbot's role in collecting feedback and making recommendations. To manage user preferences and track viewed categories and liked tags, I'll be creating a `UserPreferencesContext` or expanding the existing `ThemeContext`.


**Developing Interactive Elements**

I'm now focusing on integrating the "Өнөөдрийн мэдлэг" feature more deeply. Local storage will manage daily fact preferences, simulating a consistent habit. I've also updated the `Home.tsx` and `Sidebar.tsx` components to display this new section. Plus, I've created the `QuizCard.tsx` component for interactive quizzes, ready for integration into article detail pages. Finally, I will adjust the system instructions in the `ChatAssistant.tsx` file, as the recent updates call for it.


**Enhancing User Engagement**

I'm making a more refined personalized feed using the `UserPreferencesContext` to inject user preferences into the system prompt. I've been working on new UI elements: `QuizCard` and a more interactive `DailyKnowledge` component. My code changes include updates to several components, along with a newly created `UserPreferencesContext.tsx` to handle user history and preferences. I also added a `quiz` field in `ContentItem`, and integrated the new components into the homepage, sidebar, and detail pages.


**Prioritizing Personalization**

I've been working on simulating personalization without a backend. My strategy now involves storing visited categories in local storage and scoring mock content based on category matches. I'm also ensuring daily facts are consistently displayed each day. I've enriched the mock content with Q&A objects for the quiz feature and defined a system for tracking user interactions. I'll be adding the ability to track user preferences using a context, and the structure of mock content has been updated accordingly.


**Refining the Chatbot's Role**

Currently, I'm defining the chatbot's primary role as a question-asker and recommender, aligning with the prompt's focus. I'm exploring how to leverage the chatbot within the overall experience, especially in the context of personalized daily knowledge.  I will be writing the XML. I've also decided to integrate `DailyKnowledgeWidget` and have a design ready to go. To make "Feature 1" work, I will begin to outline some logic to shuffle content.

Based on your requirements, I will transform Channel Mongolia into an active, personalized platform.

Here is the plan:
1.  **Personalization Engine (`UserPreferencesContext`)**: A new context to track what users view and like (stored locally) to generate a "Recommended for You" feed.
2.  **Daily Knowledge Widget (`DailyKnowledge`)**: A specific interactive component for the "Daily Knowledge" feature with immediate feedback (Thumbs Up/Down), replacing the static FactBox.
3.  **Interactive Quiz (`QuizCard`)**: A new component embedded in articles to encourage active learning.
4.  **Content Updates**: Adding quiz data to the mock content and updating the Home/Detail pages to display these new features.
